_comment: Hand-maintained mapping from Perplexity's public API pages to pricing.json entries.
No model list is held here: the pages list the models.
Two pages are read. `models_source` prices the Agent API's models, one table per
maker, headed `Model | Input ($/1M) | Output ($/1M) | Cache read ($/1M)`. A model
priced in two tiers is billed at the high rates past the size its cells state:
'(<200k) / (≥200k)' publishes long_context_threshold 200000, '(≤272k) / (>272k)'
272001. 'N% off input' is a cache price worked out from the input rate, per tier.
`source`, the pricing page, carries the rates of its own pricing calculator as data
(`const[defaultPricing]=useState(()=>({...}))`): the tools, the sandbox, the Search
API, embeddings and the Decisions API. Its model rates are not read: on 2026-11-10
they lacked a model the models page lists. The tests use them as a cross-check.
`units` is what the calculator's own `_meta.units` must state, section by section,
word for word. A section stated in any other unit fails the run: tools are read as
dollars per invocation (published per thousand calls), the Search API per thousand
requests, the sandbox per session, embeddings and the Decisions API per million
tokens. `units_not_read` names the units stated for sections that are known and
not read; a unit stated for any other section is reported in the run's notes.
Not published: the `presets` (effort levels), whose token and tool counts are
median examples, not billed values, as Perplexity's note says; the Orchestrator API,
which neither page prices; and the Decisions API's output, which is free.

units.decisions.input: $ per 1,000,000 input tokens (output tokens are free; no per-request fee)
